articleTitle: Interactive customer services-improving communications with customers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Business Applications of Multimedia Communications (Digest No: 1997/064)
abstract: A research group at the University of Salford in partnership with NORWEB Communications, is involved in an EPSRC funded programme investigating the use of multimedia systems and modern telecommunications to enhance companies' customer service provision. The way organisations interact with their customers is key for success. Modern telecommunications systems offer the opportunity to exploit multimedia to deliver a whole new range of interactive on-demand services, directly to the customer within their own premises and at a time most convenient to them.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Business Applications of Multimedia Communications (Digest No: 1997/064)
abstract: In the 1980s we saw the emergence of the famous three telework practitioners: Rank Xerox, the FI Group and ICL. This article presents an overview of the status of teleworking today. Teleworking is a flexible way of working which covers a wide range of work activities, all of which entail working remotely from an employer, or from a traditional place of work. Teleworkers may be employed or self-employed. Under this arrangement telecommunications are used to link those doing the work with those commissioning it. Work may be advertised, commissioned, controlled, monitored and delivered using telecommunication networks and systems. Teleworking may be part-time or full-time and includes people working from home (e.g. consultants and programmers), people working from home (e.g. sales staff) and people working at local centres such as telecottages or neighbourhood offices.

articleTitle: The Virtual Chamber of Commerce-a GEMISIS 2000 project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Business Applications of Multimedia Communications (Digest No: 1997/064)
abstract: This paper describes the development of a project which is driven by the need to provide high quality services which small businesses will use. The project is not technology driven even though we have a leading edge capability to deliver high quality video content to large numbers of concurrent users of the services. GEMISIS 2000 is a partnership between Salford City Council, The University of Salford and NYNEX Cablecomms. The aim of GEMISIS 2000 is to develop applications of all kinds (industrial/commercial/educational/health/governmental) which make use of the NYNEX cable network being installed under their franchise in the area. The Virtual Chamber of Commerce is one of a number of projects under the GEMISIS 2000 banner part funded by the European Regional Development Fund.

articleTitle: The delivery of multimedia services for business
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Business Applications of Multimedia Communications (Digest No: 1997/064)
abstract: Summary form only given. The author provides a review of multimedia services using CD-ROM, internet/intranet, broadband based full motion video, and kiosk systems. The objective for business in introducing multimedia technology is to improve internal productivity and to gain competitive advantage externally, often through better customer service. Kiosk systems are perhaps the most obvious currently deployed example of multimedia services being used by business to address new markets. They are essentially multimedia PCs with touch activated and in some cases proximity activated video. They combine interactivity and information delivery.
